angle.selected_angle: Language Preservation Race: One Language Dies Every 40 Days—Can Atasözleri Survive?
angle.rationale: Creates immediate audience urgency via time-bound extinction rate (40 days per ELCat, corrected from 2-week misconception). Connects global statistics to specific Turkic case studies: Tuvan, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uyghur. Grounds story in documented preservation *initiatives* (not just loss abstractions).

hook.primary_hook: One Language Dies Every 40 Days—And With It, a Proverb Tradition That Took Centuries to Build
hook.entry_point: Number impact: 7,168 languages today; 43% endangered; ~1,400 with <1,000 speakers. By 2100: 3,500+ lost if status quo continues.
hook.conflict: Preservation efforts ARE happening (Wikitongues, Atalar Sözderi, UNESCO Manas). Question: Can preservation catch up to extinction?

research_foundation.readiness_rationale: Completeness 0.88 is highest in 5-cluster research. All 12 claims CORE status (8), SUPPORTING (2), PERIPHERAL (2) with detailed verdicts. Evidence quality: 3+ independent sources per major claim. Counter-arguments well-documented (extinction rate dispute: ELCat vs. UNESCO). Gaps explicitly marked (longitudinal effectiveness of documentation unproven).
key_strengths: Extinction rate data robust: 3+ independent sources per rate variant
2100 projection well-documented via UNESCO and academic sources
Language-death/proverb-loss connection supported by 5+ evidence items
Case-specific documentation: Tuvan (~130k speakers), Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uyghur all with active preservation programs
Counter-arguments captured: extinction rate disputes, documentation effectiveness uncertainty, revitalization contingency
major_gaps: Which specific Turkic proverbs have been lost? (Inventory gap)
Uyghur-specific proverb transmission loss rates (Turkish diaspora data doesn't generalize)
Longitudinal effectiveness data: does documentation (Wikitongues, Atalar Sözderi) actually slow extinction? (No long-term metrics)
Implementation metrics: Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan/Tatarstan language preservation 2024-2026 progress (data lag)
readiness_conditions: Condition A (optional): Note extinction-rate dispute — ELCat estimates 1 language every 3-4 months; older UNESCO figure claimed 1 every 2 weeks. Both are alarming rates; exact figure less important than trend.
Condition B (optional): Emphasize 2100 projection is contingent — assumes status quo; if preservation efforts scale, outcome could be 20-40% language loss instead of 50-90%.
Condition C (optional): Acknowledge documentation effectiveness unknown — Wikitongues has documented 776 languages (2,055 resources), but no data yet on whether documentation slows extinction.

content_brief.target_audience: UNESCO/cultural preservation advocates, language learners, Turkic heritage interest, general audience concerned with cultural extinction
content_brief.narrative_approach: Urgency via quantifiable rates + hope via documented preservation initiatives + scholarly caution on effectiveness
content_brief.content_warnings: Geopolitical sensitivity on Uyghur language policy (well-documented; framed as one case within broader endangered-language crisis, not as primary focus)

narrative_acts.title: Global Language Extinction Crisis (quantified)
narrative_acts.content: 7,168 languages today; 43% endangered; 1,400+ with <1,000 speakers. Extinction rates: 1 every 40 days (ELCat) or 1 every 2 weeks (disputed). By 2100: 50-90% loss projected. Visual: timeline, extinction rate graphic, speaker population maps.

narrative_acts.title: Atasözleri as Language Proxy (why proverbs matter)
narrative_acts.content: Language death = proverb tradition loss (confirmed via 5+ sources). Specific example: Latin proverbs survive in modern Romance languages, but Latin is dead. What happens when languages have no 'heir' language?

narrative_acts.title: Turkic-Specific Endangered Languages
narrative_acts.content: Tuvan (~130k speakers), Kazakh documentation (Atalar Sözderi 100-volume series), Kyrgyz traditions + Manas UNESCO recognition, Uyghur language policy context. Each case shows different preservation model: state program (Kazakhstan), academic documentation (Kyrgyz), geopolitical pressure (Uyghur).

narrative_acts.title: Preservation Initiatives & Open Questions
narrative_acts.content: Wikitongues (776 languages, 2,055 resources), UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage programs, academic paremiography research. Question: Is documentation enough? Longitudinal data lacking. Show preservation work happening; note uncertainty about scaling.

production_notes.historiographic_transparency_required: Yes — Extinction rate disputes noted (ELCat vs. UNESCO); 2100 projection contingency clarified; documentation effectiveness marked as unproven

caveats_detail: Extinction rate dispute: 'Estimates vary — ELCat suggests one language every 3-4 months; some older sources cited a faster rate. Both indicate rapid extinction.'

2100 projection contingency: 'This projection assumes current conditions continue unchanged. If language revitalization efforts scale up significantly, actual 2100 loss could be 20-40% instead of 50-90%.'
Documentation effectiveness: 'Wikitongues and similar projects have documented 776 languages globally, but no longitudinal data yet on whether documentation actually slows extinction rates.'

Uyghur specificity: 'Uyghur language policy is geopolitically contested; well-documented in international sources but interpretation varies by perspective. Frame as one case study within broader preservation crisis.'
Specific proverb inventory gap: 'While we know languages are dying, precise inventories of which Turkic proverbs have been lost (vs. documented) remain incomplete.'
